sections.summary: Mr. Gaibullodzhon Ilyasovich Saidov, a civilian, was tried by the Military Chamber of the Supreme Court, sentenced to death, and detained in harsh conditions (small cell, bucket toilet). He received limited legal assistance and minimal contact with his family.

sections.label: Issue and actual outcome
sections.summary: The author alleged violations of article 14(2) (presumption of innocence), article 14(3)(b) (right to legal representation), and article 14(3)(d) (publicity of trial). The Committee concluded that these rights were breached and found a violation of article 14, as well as article 6 (fair trial) and related provisions.

sections.label: Deciding body's reasoning
sections.summary: The Committee held that state‑directed media prejudice, the accusatory stance of the judge, and the late appointment of counsel undermined the fairness of the proceedings, constituting violations of article 14 paragraphs 2, 3(b), 3(d) and, by extension, article 6.

6.9 The Committee recalls 9 that the imposition of a senten ce of death upon conclusion of a
trial in which the provisions of the Covenant ha ve not been respected constitutes a violation of
article 6 of the Covenant.  In the current case, the sentence of death was passed, and
subsequently carried out, in violation of the right to a fair trial as set out in article 14 of the
Covenant, and therefore also in violation of article 6 of the Covenant.
7. The Human Rights Committee, acting under article 5, paragraph 4, of the Optional
Protocol to the International Covenant on Civil a nd Political Rights, is of the view that the facts
before it disclose a violation of Mr. Saidov’ s rights under articles 6, 7, 10, paragraph 1, and 14,
paragraphs 1, 2, 3 (b), (d), and (g), and 5, of the Covenant.

sections.label: General comparison factors and limits
sections.summary: The Committee noted that the case mirrors earlier communications (e.g., Kelly v. Jamaica, Conroy Levy v. Jamaica) where media influence and lack of counsel were deemed violations. It emphasized the need for states to ensure effective remedies under article 2(3)(a) and to publish the Views.
